what: The Final Grade Calculator tells you what score you need on your final exam to finish a course with the grade you want. Enter your current grade, how much the final is worth and your goal, and it works out the score needed.

A second mode lets you list every part of the course, such as assignments, quizzes, the midterm and the final, with their weights and your scores. It shows your current grade and the average you need on whatever is still to come.
It says clearly when a goal is impossible (you would need more than 100%) or already secured (you reach it even with 0). Everything runs in your browser.
uses: Know whether you need 60% or 95% on the final before you start studying.
Check if a grade is still possible
See the highest overall grade you can still reach.
Keep a scholarship or pass a course
Find the score needed to stay above a minimum grade.
Enter every category from your syllabus and watch your current grade as scores come in.
The table shows the score needed for 90%, 80%, 70%, 60% and 50% at once.
tutorial: Click "Current grade + final" if you know your grade so far, or "By category" to enter each part of the course.
In "Your current grade (%)" type your grade before the final, such as 82.
In "Final exam weight (%)" type how much of the course grade the final counts for, such as 40. You find this in your syllabus or course outline.
In "Grade you want overall (%)" type the overall grade you want. The large box shows the score you need on the final.
In "By category", enter each category's weight and score. Scores can be a percentage (85) or marks (17/20). Leave the score empty for parts not done yet, then enter your goal.
The boxes show your current grade and your overall grade if you score 0 or 100 on what is left. The table lists the score needed for common targets.
features: Needed final score = (goal − current grade × (1 − final weight)) ÷ final weight.
Any number of weighted categories, with scores as percentages or as marks like 17/20.
Clear messages when you would need over 100%, or when your goal is safe even with 0.
Your overall grade if you score 0 or 100 on everything left.
A warning when category weights do not add up to 100%.
Your categories and scores are saved in this browser for next time.

example.title: Worked example: 80% now, final worth 40%
example.text: Your current grade is 80% and the final exam is worth 40%. You want 85% overall. The part you have already earned is 80 × 0.6 = 48 points. You need 85 − 48 = 37 more points from the final, which is 37 ÷ 0.4 = 92.5%. With 0 on the final you would end on 48%, and with 100% you would end on 88%, so a goal of 90% is not possible.

tips: Use the weights from your syllabus. If the final replaces a lower midterm, or there is a pass mark on the final itself, those rules are not included.
If your current grade already counts dropped quizzes or curve adjustments, use it as it is.
In category mode, leave the scores of future work empty; do not type 0, which counts as a real zero.
Aim a few points above the score needed to allow for rounding and surprises.
Letter grade cut-offs differ; check which percentage your course uses for each letter.
problems: You would need more than 100% on the final. Lower your goal, or ask whether extra credit is available.
My weights do not add up to 100%
